proof_they_are_different_functions.test: spike injection at a non-matched candidate k*
proof_they_are_different_functions.result: matcher IGNORES the decoy and keeps reporting tau; contrast latch JUMPS to the decoy
proof_they_are_different_functions.conclusion: they agree ONLY when the matched slice is the sole anomaly, which is exactly and only the synthetic case O1 proposes

F2_fallback_claim_refuted.claim_under_test: the aggregation is not a pointwise function of each candidate slice (the prior audit's highest defensible level)
F2_fallback_claim_refuted.population: 12 random seeds x 6 permutations x 6 tau = 432 units, randomly initialised aggregation
F2_fallback_claim_refuted.conclusion: the P2 claim is a property of the ARCHITECTURE, not of training; it cannot separate a trained model from random weights
F2_fallback_claim_refuted.correction: the prior audit called this 'close to vacuous by prior probability'. It is vacuous BY MEASUREMENT.

F3_padding_objection_overstated.prior_audit_claim: the k-axis zero padding is a control mismatch
F3_padding_objection_overstated.measurement: relative cost change when the matched slice is moved to each position, random Conv3d, tau=3
F3_padding_objection_overstated.conclusion: the padded ends sit INSIDE the interior range; the asymmetry is real but not distinguishable from the generic permutation effect
F3_padding_objection_overstated.action: withdraw it as a separate defect; it does not rescue O1 either

primary_question.question: does candidate-axis permutation identify geometric correspondence, or merely sensitivity to candidate-axis ordering?
primary_question.answer: merely sensitivity to candidate-axis ordering; and by F1 not even that cleanly, since a non-matching ordering-sensitive operator gives the same signature

symmetry_note.prior_audit_argument: A(V o pi) = A(V) o pi for pointwise operators, so no pi separates two pointwise mechanisms
symmetry_note.correction: correct but NARROWER THAN THE FAILURE. HC_contrast is NOT pointwise (3-tap kernel along k) and still reproduces the signature.
symmetry_note.actual_defeating_class: every operator whose response is driven by the single degenerate slice V[tau] == 0 -- by smallness, local contrast, or outlier-ness, pointwise or convolutional

section5_identifiability_test.question: can a model with candidate-axis convolution, index dependence, arbitrary nonlinearity and arbitrary learned filters, but NO correspondence, produce a systematic S8 improvement?
section5_identifiability_test.evidence: MEASURED, with a constructed instance (HC_contrast) having all four properties, proved not a matcher, Delta_P1 = +1.787..+2.653 at E_orig = 0.840
section5_identifiability_test.what_O1_establishes_instead: that the model's output moves when the candidate content is re-indexed -- nothing more

statistic_audit.absolute_index_dependence: separates content-driven from index-driven and nothing finer
statistic_audit.sharpness_refinement: the z-score removes GLOBAL GAIN exactly; the nuisance is profile SHAPE peakedness, not scale
threshold_rejection_reasons: the scale is set by pi and tau, not by the mechanism
m_pi = E[pi^-1] is pulled toward 5.5, so a fully disrupted model looks LEAST disrupted at tau ~ 5-6
the threshold equals the method's own readout blur (~1 candidate), so it cannot resolve the effect it thresholds

counterexample_suite.standard_applied: each counterexample realized as WEIGHTS of the frozen module, with an intervention proof that it is not the mechanism under test
counterexample_suite.verdict: NOT IDENTIFIABLE -- two provably different functions give materially the same observable prediction in every column

closure_result.statement: the spike test that separates them is NOT constructible inside this pipeline under a spatially reduced statistic
closure_result.derivation: V[k,w] = Lf[w+k] - Rf[w]. A spike in Rf[w] inflates V at ALL k for that w (not candidate-selective). A spike in Lf at column c inflates V at k = c - w, which MOVES with w; across the 20-column mask the anomalous candidate takes 20 different values and the spatial median removes it.

null_and_control.null_hypothesis: Delta = 0, the output does not follow candidate content
null_and_control.permutation_arm_is: a PAIRED TREATMENT, not a null
null_and_control.random_aggregation_is: a FLOOR, degenerate (near zero for flatness, not geometric blindness)
null_and_control.unit_of_inference: UNSPECIFIED; must be at least (checkpoint, pair, tau, pi) with pi a RANDOM EFFECT
null_and_control.max_rule_forbidden_proof: P(max over N below threshold) = (1-p)^N -> 0 for any null with mass p > 0; derived here, not inherited
null_and_control.gate_can_pass_and_fail: numerically yes; interpretably no -- a pass is reproduced by HC_contrast
